title: Quiet Start — Hire Accelerator & 7-day activation checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for 'quiet starts' — hires that need a minimal visibility onboarding (small team, sensitive hires, or rapid replacements) where we prioritize fast contributor impact with reduced ceremony. Bundle: offer -> day0 -> 7-day activation.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for individual IC roles (IC2–IC5), professional services contractors, and urgent backfills when leadership requests limited cross-org broadcast.
- Not for managers, executive hires, or roles needing broad stakeholder alignment (use standard onboarding).

Success signals (first 14 days):
- Access and tooling: account + repo access granted within 8 business hours of Day0.
- First small deliverable: merge/ship or clear take-home outcome within 7 days (e.g., bugfix, infra runbook edit, short doc).
- Manager confidence: manager rates candidate >= 4/5 on the 7-day activation survey.

Pre-offer alignment (people-ops + hiring manager):
- Confirm minimal required accesses (list exact repos, GCP/Buckets, Slack channels, PagerDuty team). Keep the list to essentials only.
- Decide visibility: who gets the welcome email. Default: manager + pod. Opt-in: broader team.
- Agree an explicit 7-day deliverable and acceptance criteria (documented in the offer/onboarding note).

Offer & preboarding checklist (immediately after offer accept):
- People Ops: send compact offer packet and a 1‑page 'what to expect first week' note.
- IT/Security: initiate account provisioning ticket with priority tag "quiet-start". Include access whitelist.
- Manager: prepare 7-day deliverable, PR template, and two onboarding micro-tasks.
- Hardware: request laptop + VPN token; if delivery takes >48h shift plan to remote-access dev VM.

Day 0 (first 8 hours) manager + people-ops responsibilities:
- Manager: 30-min kick-off (team intro + outcome expectations). Keep it focused, no org history lecture.
- People Ops: confirm account + email created, add to payroll/benefits, and copy brief welcome note to manager for sending.
- IT: ensure SSH keys or SSO access and repo rights. Mark any blocked items as high priority.
- Buddy: assigned (peer IC) to shadow for the first three days and help unblock dev environment.

Day 1–3 rapid activation steps:
- Day1: environment smoke test (clone repo, install deps, run test-suite subset). Buddy runs a 1-hour pairing session.
- Day2: small bugfix or infra tweak assigned by manager; expected to open a draft PR.
- Day3: PR review & merge, or a doc-based deliverable if local environment still blocked.
- Manager: short 15-min daily sync for first 72 hours (asynchronous alternative if timezones conflict).

Day 4–7 stabilization and feedback:
- Day4–5: second micro-task that exercises a different surface area (e.g., infra vs. app code; telemetry vs. feature).
- Day6: 1:1 check-in focused on signal collection: blockers, access, unclear expectations.
- Day7: manager completes quick activation survey and either (A) greenlights full integration and wider announcement, or (B) schedules a remediation plan and asks People Ops for support.

Interview rubric adjustments for quiet-hire candidates (pre-hire expectations):
- Emphasize practical work product over cultural theater. Use a short, applied exercise that mirrors the 7-day deliverable.
- Interviewers must rate on three pillars: practical competency, ramp speed, and communication for async work. Keep rubric scalar (1–5) and require brief evidence sentence per score.
- Avoid multi-day take-homes unless candidate timebox given; prefer a 2–3 hour scoped exercise.

Communication templates (short and copyable)
- Preboarding note to candidate (example):
  Hi {{name}}, quick note — welcome to Redwood. Expect an email from IT with SSO steps and a short 'first week' PDF from your manager. Your first-week goal: ship a small PR or doc to get you comfortable with the flow. Buddy: {{buddy_name}}. Ping me if anything is delayed. —Priya

- Manager Day0 DM to team (opt-in template):
  Heads-up: we have a quiet start joining our pod on {{date}} — only sharing with pod and immediate collaborators. Please join me in supporting them, especially with environment setup.

Risk signals & contingency (people-ops + manager):
- Flag A: access not provisioned by end of Day1 -> escalate to IT lead and open "quiet-start-escalation" channel.
- Flag B: candidate cannot produce first micro deliverable by Day7 with clear blocker -> 1:1 diagnostic + remediation mini-plan (2 week).
- Flag C: candidate expresses mismatched expectations -> schedule hiring manager + recruiting + candidate call within 48 hours.

Operational guidelines & tips (notes to self):
- Keep documentation intentionally minimal: 1 pager beats long wiki for quiet starts.
- Reuse the same checklist for contractors to avoid reoriginating steps each time.
- Slack: avoid org-wide welcome threads unless manager opts in; default is pod-only.
- Use an alias for provisioning tickets (peopleops-quiet@) so IT queues can prioritize.

Templates to add to repo (follow-ups / recurring artifacts):
- One-page first week guide (manager template)
- PR starter template for 7-day micro-tasks
- Quick activation survey (3 questions)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should Legal sign off on quiet-start NDAs or do standard agreements suffice? (ask Legal: LEGAL-112)
- Can we pre-stage loaner hardware kits in SF/NY to reduce laptop lead time? (ops feasibility)
- Experiment: measure 7-day activation success rate across 20 hires and iterate checklist by role.

Quick links & references:
- Quiet start guidance (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/pages/INF-quiet-start-guidance
- Ticket template: JIRA:PEOPLE-873

Attachments to create:
- first-week-onepager-template.md
- quiet-start-provisioning-ticket-template.txt
- activation-survey-google-form (link to be created)

Notes: this is a working doc — expect edits after 3 pilot hires. Keep the language pragmatic and avoid extra approvals.
